radiology_report:
Antoni van Leeuwenhoek
Department of Radiology
Date: 24 Nov 2024
Exam: mpMRI prostate

Clinical indication: PSA 3.9 ng/mL, rising trend, prior biopsy Gleason 3+5. Request for staging and lesion characterization.

FINDINGS:
Prostate volume: 31.47 mL.
T2-weighted imaging reveals a focal, ill-defined hypo-intense lesion within the left peripheral zone, approximately 18 mm in maximal dimension, abutting the anterior capsule and demonstrating indistinct margins suggestive of extracapsular extension. Diffusion-weighted imaging shows marked restricted diffusion in the corresponding region with high signal on high b-value images and low ADC values. Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences demonstrate early, intense enhancement of the lesion relative to surrounding glandular tissue. No suspicious lymphadenopathy or bone marrow replacement is identified.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS v2.1 category 5 lesion in the left peripheral zone.
PSA density: 0.124 ng/mL/mL.
Clinical T stage: cT3 based on imaging features.
csPCa predicted probability 0.7731299.

previous_notes.text:
16 Jul 2023 - Dr. T. Hendriks (GP):
Patient returned for routine PSA monitoring. Result was 2.7 ng/mL, showing a gradual increase from the previous value of 2.3 ng/mL in April 2022. Discussed the slow rise and the need for continued surveillance. Advised repeat testing in approximately 12 months and maintained current watchful approach without immediate urological referral.

previous_notes.author: Dr. T. Hendriks (GP)
previous_notes.text:
11 May 2024 - Dr. T. Hendriks (GP):
PSA re-evaluation showed further elevation to 3.3 ng/mL. Patient reported no new urinary symptoms but expressed concern about the rising trend. Given the persistent increase and the patient's age, a referral to urology was initiated for further assessment and potential biopsy discussion. Patient informed about the referral process and asked to bring all previous lab results to the specialist appointment.

pathology_report:
Biopsy timepoint 1 (11 May 2024):
Histological examination of the prostate tissue specimens reveals acinar adenocarcinoma. The Gleason score is 3+5, corresponding to ISUP grade group 4. Perineural invasion is identified. The tumour is located in the left side of the prostate. No cribriform or intraductal patterns are identified.

Summary of trajectory:
The histological grade group remains consistent at ISUP 4 across the available biopsy timepoint, with persistent perineural invasion.

AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology): grade group 4.
